text:
New Jersey needed overtime to beat Detroit, but the play suggested it should never have been that close. The Devils created 4.51 expected goals to Detroit's 2.25 and won 83 percent of the simulated replays, and they took 72 shot attempts to the Red Wings' 55. It was 5-4 at Little Caesars Arena because Jake Allen let in 1.8 goals more than the 27 shots against him deserved.

The first period was close to a one-way game, with New Jersey out-chancing Detroit 1.83 to 0.26 in expected goals. Evan Rodrigues scored first, and Emmitt Finnie tied it late on a 6 percent look. The second period was the wild one. Michael Brandsegg-Nygård put Detroit ahead, Anthony Mantha tied it on a 2 percent chance, and Nico Hischier scored on the power play with a tip-in. Alex DeBrincat answered for 3-3, and Jesper Bratt restored the lead with 68 seconds left in the period. John Gibson faced a 57 percent look from Jack Hughes in the second and stopped it.

DeBrincat tied it again at 4-4 early in the third, his second goal of the night, and Detroit was the better side in that period, 0.80 to 0.49 in expected goals. The extra frame was short. Hughes, who put eight shots on goal and finished with a goal and two assists, scored 1:19 into overtime off a Bratt pass. Hughes was the first star, with DeBrincat second and Bratt third.
